dependencies.name: analysis-target
dependencies.summary: a real project for the CLI to analyze — the subject every analysis flow reaches its verdict against

registration.description: path to a checked-out project on this machine; it is COPIED into the sandbox, so the run never touches the original

needs.need: a project the deterministic scan finds at least one violation in EVERY category the analyze report names — Code quality, Security, Bugs, Architecture, Performance, Reliability, Database and Style — and whose sources include TypeScript (.ts), JavaScript (.js) and Python (.py) files

more than 20 deterministic findings, so the default listing is a partial twenty-wide window with a next-page pointer and `--all` is visibly a different shape, plus at least one critical-or-high finding and at least one below it so the severity filter has something to leave out
more than 20 deterministic findings, so the default listing paginates and `--all` can be told apart from it, plus at least one critical-or-high finding alongside at least one of a lower severity
at least one deterministic finding, so a severity-filtered listing renders its violation count instead of the empty state
at least one source file the LLM rules accept, so the run reports a non-zero file count, and at least one deterministic finding so the baseline run's violation summary is not empty
at least one source file the LLM rules accept, so the run reports a non-zero file count, and at least one deterministic finding so the violation summary is not empty

dependencies.name: claude-login
dependencies.summary: an authenticated Claude Code installation — a long-lived token from `claude setup-token`, the state `claude -p` needs before it will answer

condition.sentence: only when the LLM transport is `claude-code`; the `api` transport reaches the model with a key instead

vars.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
vars.description: a long-lived token from `claude setup-token`; it is exported into the sandbox child, so the spawned `claude` authenticates with it and your real login state is never read or touched

needs.need: a long-lived token from `claude setup-token` that answers a non-interactive `claude -p` prompt without prompting for authentication
a token that answers the relevance, area-tag and overlap stages of one full `spec scan` — a scan has no `--no-llm`, so without it the flow reaches no corpus at all
a token that passes the scan's up-front `claude` login probe, which runs before the estimate and aborts the run when it fails
a token with enough remaining quota for two full scans of the same document set in one session
a token for the initial scan and for the re-scan each `spec docs include`/`exclude` triggers (cached docs cost nothing, the two written probes do)
a token for the two scans that fold the fetched site pages into the corpus
a token for the scan that flags the overlaps and for the re-scan the recorded verdicts must survive
a token for one scan over a small seeded document tree — discovery is deterministic, but the scan that publishes its result still runs the LLM stages
a token for three scans over a small seeded tree, one per include-scope setting
a token for one scan over a small seeded tree of OpenAPI documents and their markdown neighbours
a token for the login probe every generate runs, plus the relevance and area-tag calls the one force-included document costs
a token with enough remaining quota for ONE full guard generate over the bound corpus — claim extraction, flow synthesis, authoring, fidelity and triage
a token that answers the login probe setup runs before any work, twice in one session
a token that passes the login probe generate runs before it looks for a recipe — the run stops at the recipe gate, so nothing else is spent
a token that answers the login probe setup runs before each of this flow’s three detection passes

dependencies.name: llm-api-credentials
dependencies.summary: a provider API account the CLI can reach the model through directly

condition.sentence: only when the LLM transport is `api`; the `claude-code` transport uses a local login instead

vars.name: provider
vars.description: the provider id `truecourse config llm setup --provider` is given (anthropic | openai | bedrock | copilot)

vars.name: model
vars.description: a model id that provider serves, as `--model` takes it

vars.name: api-key
vars.description: an API key for that provider with enough quota to complete one analysis

vars.name: base-url
vars.description: the provider API base URL — omit for the provider default

needs.need: a key whose live provider probe succeeds, because `config llm setup` verifies the account before it saves anything
a key whose live provider probe succeeds (`config llm setup` verifies the account before it saves anything) with enough quota for one full spec scan
a key whose live provider probe succeeds (`config llm setup` verifies the account before it saves anything) with enough quota for one full guard generate

dependencies.name: dotnet-sdk
dependencies.summary: the built C# Roslyn semantic host — without it, analyzing C# fails hard by design (there is no tree-sitter-only fallback)

condition.sentence: only when the analyzed project contains C#

vars.name: TRUECOURSE_ROSLYN_HOST
vars.description: absolute path to the built host (`dotnet build -c Release tools/csharp-roslyn-host`), which needs the .NET 8 SDK once per checkout

dependencies.name: spec-docs-project
dependencies.summary: a real documentation project for `truecourse spec scan` to curate — the document set every corpus-quality verdict in the spec-consolidation area is reached against

registration.description: path to a checked-out project on this machine that carries real documentation (PRDs, ADRs, design notes, a docs site); it is COPIED into the sandbox, so the run never touches the original

needs.need: a documentation set the scan keeps at least one doc from and groups into areas, with at least one flagged within-area overlap and at least one area holding two or more docs that do NOT disagree; it must carry no committed `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json` and no `spec.include` scope, so the first scan starts cold over the whole document set
enough uncached documentation that the pre-flight estimate has at least one stage — an estimate with no stages skips the confirm entirely, and the confirm is what this flow is about

a documentation set small enough for two full scans in one session, and unchanged between them, so the immediate re-scan can report "Nothing changed" and the estimate after one added doc can report "1 of N docs changed"
at least one document the scan keeps, so the run reports a non-zero kept count alongside the task-list document this flow writes and expects dropped
at least one flagged within-area overlap, so a conflict verdict can be recorded next to the include and exclude overrides that `specs/decisions.json` must hold together
at least THREE flagged within-area overlaps — one dismissed on its own, two more dismissed in a single bulk command — plus at least one area holding two or more docs that do not disagree

the same product the registered llms-txt-site documents (the two fixtures are a pair), at least one kept doc under docs/ and at least one kept doc at the repo root — the scope-exemption step narrows the scan to docs/** and needs a root doc to fall out

dependencies.name: llms-txt-site
dependencies.summary: a live documentation website that publishes an llms.txt index — the one spec source the engine reaches over the network, and never one it may invent

vars.name: llms-txt-url
vars.description: the absolute URL of a documentation site's llms.txt; `spec source add` reads it and fetches every same-origin markdown page it lists

vars.name: second-llms-txt-url
vars.description: the absolute URL of a SECOND llms.txt index on the same or another site — the refresh-all flow needs two registered sources, and one index yields one source

vars.name: no-llms-txt-url
vars.description: an absolute URL on a site that answers but publishes NO llms.txt index — the negative case the refusal is measured against, so "unsupported" is told apart from "unreachable"

needs.need: an llms.txt index whose same-origin links all resolve to markdown, so the fetch writes at least one page and records no `fetch-failed` skip; the pages must describe the SAME PRODUCT as the registered spec-docs-project fixture, so the scan keeps them as that repo's own documentation

an llms.txt index that lists at least one off-origin link and at least one same-origin page with no markdown form, so both recorded skip reasons (`external-origin`, `not-markdown`) have something to be true about
a `no-llms-txt-url` that answers over HTTP but serves no llms.txt index, so the refusal is a missing index rather than a missing host

TWO llms.txt indexes (the main one and second-llms-txt-url), each registering as its own source, and a site that tolerates being fetched three times in one run (two registrations, then a refresh of both) without rate-limiting the fetch into failure

dependencies.name: guard-subject-project
dependencies.summary: a repository already carried through `spec scan` and `guard setup` — the subject guard is pointed AT, and the one thing a guard flow can never fabricate: a real spec corpus and a recipe that really builds

registration.description: path to a checked-out project on this machine that has been through `truecourse spec scan`, `truecourse guard setup` and `truecourse guard generate` at least once; it is COPIED into the sandbox in full (gitignored files included), so the run never touches the original

needs.need: its `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json`, `specs/decisions.json`, `scenarios/recipe.json`, `scenarios/manifest.json` and scenario YAMLs COMMITTED to git, and a recipe whose build succeeds in a sandbox so the run this flow makes reaches its scenarios and leaves a transcript behind

a `scenarios/manifest.json`, a `scenarios/flows.json` and a `guard/result.json` left by its last local `guard generate` — the result record is gitignored, so a fresh clone must generate once before being registered

a corpus whose last generate settled every flow, so an immediate re-generate can honestly report that nothing changed, and a repository the scan admits one more markdown document into through `spec docs include`

a spec corpus small enough that ONE full authoring pass finishes inside the hour a step may take, a recipe whose install and build succeed in a sandbox and whose `entry` starts, and at least one third-party SDK import or `https://` URL literal in its sources so the generate record’s detected-service list is non-empty
the same prepared repository, small enough that a SECOND full authoring pass fits the step budget on the api transport

a SIMPLE single-app repository — one committed lockfile, one build script, one `bin` entry — so the deterministic proposer settles the recipe with no LLM call, and whose install, build and entrypoint really run in a sandbox
a committed `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json`, so a generate run with the recipe removed stops on the missing preparation rather than for want of documents

a committed `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json` (setup refuses to run without one) and a `recipe.json` with no `api` block, so the three setup runs this flow makes reach the detection step without deriving or verifying anything
